title: Graceful labelings of spiders with three-edge legs and pendant leaves at the center
summary: A graph $G$ on $m$ edges is graceful if there is an injection $f : V(G) \to \{0, 1, \ldots, m\}$ whose induced edge labels $\{|f(u) - f(v)| : uv \in E(G)\}$ are exactly $\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$. Ringel and Kotzig conjectured in 1964 that every tree is graceful. A computer check has confirmed this for all trees on at most 35 vertices (Fang 2010), but no general proof is known. Here we exhibit an infinite family of trees that escapes the named spider results of Bahls--Lake--Wertheim, Panpa--Poomsa-ard, and Panpa--Imnang--Wasuanankul: the family $T(k, m)$ of spiders with $k$ legs of length $3$…
